title: The 2010-2022 south-east minus north runoff contrast stayed inside the earlier range in a fixed 19-gauge panel
abstract: We test whether the recent runoff contrast between south-east and northern eastern Australia exceeds its earlier range. We use published 13-year rainfall-runoff model summaries and keep 13 south-east and six North gauges fixed across 38 historical windows and 2010-2022. The recent south-east minus North contrast was -29.13 percentage points. The historical minimum was -38.93 points in 1947-1959. The gap was +9.80 points, with a conditional 95% spatial cell interval of -15.85 to +55.03. Seasonal rain, longer rain memory and 150 km station rain checks also put the recent sample contrast inside its earlier range. A 100 km station check failed coverage. With the same 19 gauges but historical starts restricted to 1957 onward, the recent contrast fell 16.71 points below the historical minimum. Thus the historical start date changes the sample record claim. Both regions had high runoff efficiency in the early minimum, whereas the recent departures straddled zero. This is not evidence of the same physical state or cause. Few cells, source fit differences, dependent windows and selected long records limit inference. We do not test the full post-1997 duration. Code, licensed aggregate inputs, exact hashes, draws and an independent audit are supplied.

display.caption: Fixed gauge panels and the gap between recent and minimum historical regional contrast. All primary spatial intervals include zero.

citations.reason: Six published aggregate window tables; we add a fixed-panel regional contrast and start-date comparison.
